corrections.why: The Register and the 2020 report say the steel tower was erected in 1933. Neither says it replaced an earlier steel tower; the earlier structure was wooden.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 9,991 ft (3,045 m) and Wikipedia gives 10,020 ft (3,050 m). The record keeps the Register figure; the sources read do not settle it.

Wikipedia gives 1925 for one or both of the tower and cabin; the Register dates the log cabin to 1925 and the steel tower to 1933. A May 1915 newspaper item mentions a fire lookout tower on the peak, earlier than the Register's early-1920s wooden tower. The earliest date stays open.
The Forest Lookouts page and the FFLA New Mexico listing give Grant County; the Register and Wikipedia give Sierra County. The record keeps Sierra.
The Register gives 45.9 ft and the 2020 report gives 45 ft. The record uses the Register figure, converted to 14.0 m.

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree across sources: the Register's 1933 tower and 1925 cabin, Wikipedia's 1925 date for one or both of tower and cabin, and a May 1915 newspaper mention of a lookout tower. Story says so. Access level 'public' refers only to the overnight log cabin, per a single Wikipedia sentence; please verify before publishing and do not read it as tower access. No staffing source found; staffing omitted. Brief design said 45-ft; Register says 45.9 ft (height_m 14.0 converted). Brief's 1933 'replaced' moved to corrections. Brief county (Sierra) confirmed; the FFLA listing and Forest Lookouts page say Grant. Wikipedia elevation differs from the Register. No photos added. The 2020 report's apostrophes are curly.
